information.description:
Blitzers are best described as Dragons that like to get in close. They’re also generally described as insane fanatics that devote themselves fully to the Tygers, typically acting like local hotspots of ‘gang loyalty encouragement.’ Blitzers are extremely deadly threats in combat, and will not hesitant to show you exactly how they got their nickname.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Tyger Claws).

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.

You'll meet plenty of these in Night City. Chances are even your next-door neighbor keeps one under their couch just in case. In spite of its age, it's still used by the NCPD, as well as a number of gangs. It's not hard to see why the Tactician is so widely admired. It's a cheap, simple and user-friendly weapon that can also deal an impressive amount of damage. Additional features? None. Sometimes simpler is better. Why have tagliatelle alla truffe when you can have mac 'n' cheese?

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog).

Cost: 250eb (Expensive) ♦ Required Slots: 0

Fits: All weapons capable of firing Slugs and/or Shells

You don't need special sights, rifling, or smartlinks to ensure a target drops — you need a bigger tube to fire your slugs and buckshot out of.

Attaching this attachment requires a DV17 Weaponstech Skill Check. Only one Shotgun Rechamber may be installed. Once installed, this attachment can not be uninstalled. When installed, the weapon's Single Shot and Shotgun Shell damage is increased by 1d6, to a maximum of 5d6 in either mode (Unless its base damage is higher, in which case that takes over and is not increased). Unless installed in cyberware, the weapon must now be wielded in two hands to fire, even if it was previously a one-handed weapon.

Attachment slots: 0

Foundry notes:

  • Change the weapon's damage by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Attachment Catalog > Internal Components).

Single-optic Cybereye visor that takes the place of two meat eyes. Too large for a MultiOptic Mount.

Cybereye Options are always "paired" even if there is only one of each type. Penalties from Lost Eye Critical Injury are doubled if the target solely relies on the Monovision for sight.

Borgware.
Must be paired. Ignore any vision penalties due to lighting or fog/smoke.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

The modern Kerenzikov takes the place of the now defunct Reflex Co-Processor to help reduce the strain on the user's Neuroport.

Neuralware. The user can now dodge Ranged Attacks if they could not do so already, and gain a +2 bonus to Checks for noticing Ambushes.

NOTE: Credit to Infernox_Ratchet for the basis of this item.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Kerenzikov; use this one instead of the core item.
  • The +2 is on Perception and situational, because it only applies to noticing an Ambush: tick it in the roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

If you want to stay in the game, you’re going to need a boost.

Kerenzikov Cyberware Enhancement. The Kerenzikov now counts as Speedware and also provides a +2 bonus to initiative at all times. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Enhances: Kerenzikov
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • The +2 initiative isn't automated from an upgrade; add it to the Kerenzikov as an Active Effect (bonuses.initiative) or apply it by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).
